summary: A harness.usage response_rollup series replicates its first reading, the last reading of each UTC hour once that hour is over, and its final totals when the seat ends, instead of every five minutes and at every turn end; the seat's host still reads its newest totals

replay.detail: Fewer harness.usage claims are written. A response_rollup reading after the series' first stays pending in the host's local observation log. It replicates when a later reading of the series falls in a later UTC hour (by observed_at_unix_ms), when a re-stamp of the resting seat arrives after its hour, when the seat reports ended or indeterminate, or when its step is completed, failed or released (the run is judged on its origin, and a loop's token budget reads the seat's replicated usage then). A reading after the seat ended, or from a replaced incarnation, replicates at once. The hourly local observation trim first replicates any held rollup whose hour is over, and never deletes a reading a usage slot still waits on. Turn ends and the five-minute interval no longer replicate rollups. Context occupancy, cumulative and response readings keep the existing rules. Old claims are untouched.

schema.detail: No schema change: pending rollups use the existing local_latest_slots.pending_local_id.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged. Retention already keeps the last rollup of each UTC hour (usage_series_keep), which is what now replicates.

compatibility.detail: Contract C2 of the db-breakup plan, approved: usage periods are exact to the hour. On the seat's host, st usage, /v1/usage and /v1/client/usage also count every reading since each series' last replication, and the agent, mission and run cards fold the newest, so current totals and any period boundary since then stay exact. Older boundaries inside an hour read the hour's replicated snapshots, on the host as on every other member; other members' current totals lag by up to about an hour. Per-response detail is in OTLP. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI shape changes; an older node keeps replicating rollups on its old schedule, and every node reads both.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting replicates each pending rollup at its seat's next turn end or interval; the readings stay in each host's local observation log meanwhile.
